doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Woody Herman, Chubby Jackson and Europe
title: Arrangers Neal Hefti and Johnny Mandel and their TV theme royalties
summary: He lists the band's arrangers; Mandel wrote 'MASH' and Hefti the Odd Couple and Batman themes.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah, you were playing some great arrangements, huh?

Shorty Rogers, Ralph Burns, Johnny Mandel, you name it. Neal Hefti. You go down the list of guys. Two of my close friends, Neal Hefti, and Johnny Mandel even more than Neal because I sort of grew up with Johnny, he was my roommate on the Buddy Rich band, they make so much money on — not so much on the songs that they wrote that are popular like for example “The Shadow of Your Smile,” “Emily,” “A Time for Love,” that Johnny Mandel wrote and Neal wrote “Cute” and “L’il Darling” and all these things — they wrote theme songs for two of the biggest shows that are being played all over the world now. Neal wrote the Odd Couple theme song, and Johnny wrote “MASH.” So that goes on, the royalties come in for that every time, all over the world, that keeps being played.
And they’re both good guys so I’m happy for both of them.
Yeah. A lot of — sometimes the names that would show up as you watch those things would really surprise me. Like I’m forgetting who did Batman.

You know what, he told me a lot of this recently. Now the Odd Couple is being played, every time I’m in Europe, you name it, anywhere, I see it all the time — but he told me he makes more money from Batman. And he’s such a giant arranger. And harmonically he could write. Batman is the dumbest thing, it’s like one note, Batman. And he made a fortune.
Well it fit the TV show for sure.
Oh yeah. He knew what he was doing.
